options.text: The energy stored in an object because of its height
The energy an object has because of its temperature
The energy an object has because of its motion
The force that holds two objects together

items.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because of its motion. The faster an object moves, the more kinetic energy it has.

items.stem: When an object's kinetic energy changes, what must have happened?

options.text: The object created new energy on its own
Energy was transferred to or from the object
The object's mass disappeared
Energy was destroyed

items.explanation: Energy is not created or destroyed. A change in kinetic energy is the sign that energy was transferred to or from the object.

items.stem: A pitched baseball leaves the bat faster than it arrived. Where did the extra motion come from?

options.text: Energy transferred from the swinging bat to the ball
The ball created new energy at the moment of contact
The air pushed the ball forward on its own
The ball's energy disappeared and then returned

items.explanation: The swinging bat carries kinetic energy. During the collision, some of that energy transfers to the ball, so the ball speeds up.

items.stem: A rolling soccer ball slows down and stops on the grass. What best explains this?

options.text: The ball simply ran out of its own energy supply
Kinetic energy was created by the grass
The ball's mass decreased as it rolled
Energy transferred from the ball to the ground and air

items.explanation: The ball slowed, so its kinetic energy decreased. That energy did not vanish; it transferred to the ground and air through friction.

items.stem: Which observation is the best evidence that energy was transferred to an object?

options.text: The object stayed exactly the same
The object's speed increased
The object changed color
The object got older over time

items.explanation: An increase in speed means an increase in kinetic energy, which is direct evidence that energy was transferred into the object.

items.stem: Two billiard balls collide. The cue ball slows and the second ball speeds up. This best shows that...

options.text: energy was created in the collision
only the cue ball ever had energy
energy transferred from the cue ball to the second ball
neither ball had any kinetic energy

items.explanation: The cue ball lost kinetic energy (it slowed) and the second ball gained kinetic energy (it sped up). Energy transferred from one to the other.

items.stem: A skateboarder speeds up while rolling down a ramp. Which claim is best supported by the evidence?

options.text: Kinetic energy increased because the speed increased
Kinetic energy stayed the same the whole way down
Energy was destroyed during the ride
The skateboard created brand new energy

items.explanation: The skateboarder's speed increased, so kinetic energy increased. A gain in kinetic energy is evidence that energy was transferred to the skateboarder.

items.stem: In the bat-and-ball example, what is the "system" scientists choose to study?

options.text: Only the baseball by itself
Only the bat by itself
The crowd watching the game
The bat and the baseball studied together

items.explanation: A system is the group of objects you study together. Here the system is the bat and the ball, which lets you track energy moving from one to the other.

items.stem: Which statement correctly connects force and energy transfer in a collision?

options.text: Forces have nothing to do with energy transfer
The push between objects during contact transfers energy
Energy transfers only when objects never touch
A force always destroys kinetic energy

items.explanation: During a collision the objects push on each other. That force acting during contact is how kinetic energy moves from one object to the other.

items.stem: A student claims, "Energy was transferred to the ball." What is the strongest evidence for this claim?

options.text: The ball is round and white
The game was played outdoors
The ball's speed changed after contact
The bat is made of wood

items.explanation: A measured change in the ball's speed shows its kinetic energy changed, which is the strongest evidence that energy was transferred to it.
